name: Bleomycin
route_note: IV, IM or SC injection; intrapleural for malignant effusions; intralesional in some uses
originator: Institute of Microbial Chemistry, Tokyo (Hamao Umezawa); developed by Nippon Kayaku

discovery.by: Hamao Umezawa and colleagues, Institute of Microbial Chemistry, Tokyo
discovery.note: Isolated from Streptomyces verticillus as a mixture of related glycopeptides.

tagline: Streptomyces glycopeptide that cuts DNA; key to curative testicular and Hodgkin regimens
summary: Bleomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic that chelates iron and generates free radicals that break DNA strands. It is a component of curative regimens for testicular cancer (BEP) and Hodgkin lymphoma (ABVD); it causes little marrow suppression but can cause serious pulmonary fibrosis.
mechanism: Bleomycin binds DNA through its bithiazole tail and chelates Fe(II) with its metal-binding domain. In the presence of oxygen the complex forms activated bleomycin, which abstracts hydrogen from deoxyribose and produces single- and double-strand breaks, mainly in G2 and M phase.
Bleomycin hydrolase inactivates the drug; lung and skin have low levels of this enzyme, which explains why toxicity concentrates in those tissues.
uses: Squamous cell carcinomas of head and neck, skin, cervix and vulva
Off-label: intralesional treatment of warts and vascular malformations

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Umezawa reports bleomycin from Streptomyces verticillus.

history.title: Japanese approval
history.detail: Marketed in Japan by Nippon Kayaku.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Blenoxane (Bristol).

history.title: ABVD
history.detail: Bonadonna's ABVD regimen for Hodgkin lymphoma includes bleomycin.

history.title: Testicular cancer
history.detail: Bleomycin is part of Einhorn's curative PVB regimen, later BEP.

history.title: RATHL
history.detail: The RATHL trial shows bleomycin can be omitted in Hodgkin lymphoma with a negative interim PET, reducing lung toxicity.

pk.half_life: about 2 hours with normal renal function; prolonged in renal impairment

serious: idiosyncratic reaction (hypotension, fever, wheeze) in lymphoma patients
safety.boxed_warning: Boxed warning for pulmonary fibrosis and severe idiosyncratic reactions, especially in lymphoma patients.

facts: Lung toxicity risk rises above a cumulative dose of about 400 units and with high inspired oxygen concentrations, which matters during later anaesthesia.
